ticket.title: S17 product video: Remotion, generated scenes, 7 chapters, CC0 music
ticket.description:
Design design-e963c656f5 §4.17 v22 (owner m-26ffec400f, m-f2ce5f4f14, m-767dd93f62; scope approved in m-81bb4cca5e).

**Medium:** Remotion (`npx skills add remotion-dev/skills` for the seat). The project lives in `docs/video/`, outside every shipped package. It renders an MP4 and also plays live through `@remotion/player` (the S15 site embeds it). Add a NOTICE/README line on the Remotion licence: free for individuals and companies of 3 or fewer people.

**No host screenshots** (owner: "screenshots of my machine or the tickets I am working on wont be attractive"):
- Every scene is motion graphics drawn in code in the Heronry palette (`v8/assets/brand/heronry/palettes.json`; S7 has committed the assets).
- Illustrated art comes from a spawned codex seat (image_gen per guides/codex-images.md), in the Heronry and board-avatar cartoon style. The style references are `v8/assets/brand/heronry/` and `web/src/components/agentAvatars.ts`.
- Any board UI is a stylised mock with invented demo data. No real names, paths or ticket ids anywhere.

**Chapters, in this order (60–90 s):**
1. The pool spawns seats (claude, codex, pi) as live shells.
2. The broker carries messages between seats.
3. Reactive subscriptions: seats sleep on their feed and wake only on what concerns them.
4. Context engineering: a bounded context pack, context_delta cursors, recall, and linked strategy docs.
5. The self-improving memory loop: pain → lesson → harvest → recall into the next seat.
6. One epic walking the board automatically: drafted → designed → signed_off → in_progress → in_review → done "auto: all verdicts passed".
7. Close: the Heronry logo, the tagline and the download link.

Read the real code for each mechanism so the story it tells is true: edp-pool, edp-broker, edp8 feed_driver/context/context_delta, the pain, harvest and learn skills, and board.py transitions.

**Music:** a no-copyright track (CC0 / public domain, e.g. FreePD, or a no-attribution licence). Record the source URL and licence in `docs/video/CREDITS.md`. If the seat cannot download a track, ask the owner to drop one in; do not synthesize.

**Owner checkpoints are two `demo` gates on this story.**
1. Write the storyboard doc (one still or frame sketch per chapter plus captions and a code pointer per chapter). Then `gate_open(demo)` with a note carrying the direct `/ui/doc/<id>` link and "press Approve on the demo card". Wait for the answer before rendering the full cut.
2. Build and render. Upload the MP4 and the hero loop as artifacts. Then `gate_open(demo)` again with the artifact links.

**Outputs:**
- `heronry-demo.mp4` (1080p)
- `hero.webp`, a ≤8 s loop, with a gif fallback
- `poster.png`
- 3 stills for the README (S18)

Commit the sources by path. Keep large renders out of git (attach them to the Release in S9) unless they are under 5 MB. Keep the full web e2e suite off this host. No consult.

The owner approved it through a `demo` gate on this story, opened by the engineer with a direct link, before the full cut was rendered. Every scene is generated (no host screenshots, no real names, paths or ticket ids).

`docs/video/` renders `heronry-demo.mp4` with one command. ffprobe shows 1920x1080 video, a 60–95 s duration and an audio stream. It also renders the ≤8 s `hero.webp` loop (with a gif fallback), `poster.png` and 3 README stills. `@remotion/player` plays the same composition in a page that S15 can embed. `docs/video/CREDITS.md` names the music source URL and a CC0, public-domain or no-attribution licence, plus the Remotion licence note. The PII grep (user-profile path, `C:\Projects`, owner username and email) over `docs/video/` and the renders returns 0.

Final-cut checkpoint: the MP4 is uploaded as a video artifact that plays inline on the board (task t-f01372d361). Until that task is live after the owner's board restart, a zip of the MP4 plus an inline animated-webp preview is acceptable. The hero loop is uploaded as an image artifact. The owner approved the cut through a second `demo` gate on this story. Each chapter's claim matches the code, with a pointer per chapter (for example pool spawn → edp-pool spawner, the wake → feed_driver, auto-done → board.py criteria_auto_done) listed in the storyboard doc.

ticket.title: Board plays video artifacts: accept mp4/webm upload, inline player
ticket.description:
From m-ce21682c2a: the board's upload refuses video ("allowed: images, pdf, text, markdown, json, log, zip, svg"), so the owner can only review the S17 cut as a zip to download and unpack. Owners review demo gates in the board, so the board must play video inline.

- `/v1/artifacts/upload` accepts `video/mp4` and `video/webm`, detected from magic bytes (ftyp / EBML), within the existing size cap. Raise the cap only if 100 MB does not fit a 90 s 1080p render; state the cap you choose.
- `/v1/artifacts/<id>/content` serves the correct Content-Type and supports HTTP Range requests, so the browser can seek.
- The SPA renders a video artifact as `<video controls preload="metadata">` wherever image artifacts render inline (thread attachments, doc markdown `![](…/content)`, the gate card). VS Code renders a link.
- Tests: pytest for upload acceptance and rejection (a renamed .exe posing as .mp4 is refused), Range 206, and Content-Type; vitest for the player render.

The change goes live on the owner's board restart; say so in the hand-off. No consult.
